phase_assessment.claim: The initial affirmative presentation block and its interface-understanding check were admitted. The learner observed the eight worked pairs and made the expected selection on the check, but this is only early interface evidence in an incomplete run.

Affirmative controlled practice was interrupted after five of eight original base items. Cup, plate, spoon, and bowl were selected correctly; fork was selected as knife. No gate score exists because the remaining three base items were never admitted.

PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch for the failed fork item was admitted at sequence 30, but the first replay teacher turn was invalid and the entire brokered replay exchange was rejected atomically. No replay exposure and no cold-retest response entered the canonical log.

The harness froze the run at sequence 31 because the rejected replay declared the affirmative phase for a presentation exercise. The rejected turn also failed the required exact replay realization in delivery mode, text, and script reference. The alarm records admitted_from_exchange=0.
Negative, W-question, OR-question, mixed-practice, picture-book, comprehension, transfer, and closing-recap phases were not reached and therefore were not demonstrated.

learner_capability_hypotheses.claim: No lesson-level capability for the eight table-object labels can be inferred from this incomplete alarm-frozen run. Four correct early selections and one fork-to-knife error do not establish controlled completion, mixed retrieval, transfer, or retention.
Recovery after the fork-to-knife error is not demonstrated because the replay and cold retest were never admitted.
Story comprehension, unseen-photo transfer, closing retrieval, and delayed retention are not demonstrated because conduct froze before those phases.

remaining_difficulties.claim: The learner's response to fork remediation remains wholly unknown: the only admitted fork base attempt selected knife, and no valid replay or unscored cold retest followed.
Performance on the remaining affirmative items and every later required phase remains untested.

The conductor did not realize the frozen PRESENT_AGAIN replay correctly: it supplied the presentation exercise under the affirmative phase and used an invalid machine-control delivery, generic WORKED_affirmative text, and non-exact script reference instead of the mapped single-label presentation turn.

uncertainties: The run is too incomplete to distinguish learner difficulty from a single ordinary early error; no item, gate, mixed, story, transfer, recap, or retention conclusion should be promoted.
The malformed replay was rejected with admitted_from_exchange=0, so there is no evidence about how the learner would have responded to a valid replay or cold retest.

The frozen lesson dispatch itself names the affirmative gate, affirmative presentation ID, target fork, and mapped cold-retest ID; the available evidence points to conductor realization rather than an ambiguous lesson dispatch.

The broker linted the PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch but did not independently lint the replay and cold-retest artifacts before attempted admission. This orchestration gap allowed a preventable malformed exchange to reach the harness; the harness nevertheless rejected it atomically and preserved log integrity.
The incomplete trace cannot evaluate the full lesson's dosage thresholds, picture-book teaching value, transfer quality, or FINISH predicate.
This rehearsal cannot advance actual learner state.

intervention_assessment.claim: Calling PRESENT_AGAIN after the incorrect fork base selection was the correct licensed intervention, and the dispatch arguments at sequence 30 matched the frozen target, presentation, gate, and cold-retest mapping.

The intervention execution failed immediately after dispatch. The proposed replay did not satisfy the frozen replay contract, was rejected atomically, and triggered the terminal harness alarm before any replay or cold retest was exposed.
TRAIN_MORE, TRAIN_LONGER, REPLAY_LESSON, and FINISH were not reached and cannot be judged from this run.
ALARM was correctly enforced by the harness because continuing after an invalid phase/exercise pairing would have broken the frozen intervention and phase contracts.

teacher_self_critique: I selected the right protocol-level intervention after the fork error, but failed to serialize its first required replay turn exactly. A valid replay needed the mapped affirmative presentation item for fork in the presentation phase, with the exact frozen delivery, text, and script reference, before the separate mapped cold retest.

I treated the presentation block as a generic WORKED_affirmative machine action instead of extracting the one exact frozen teacher turn required by the failed-label dispatch. That changed multiple coupled fields at once and made the artifact inadmissible.

I should have produced the intervention as smaller independently checkable tasks: first the PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch; second one exact replay teacher turn copied from the mapped presentation item and linted; third the exact cold-retest teacher artifact and lint; only then should each bounded exchange have been offered for admission.

The broker's orchestration also needs correction: linting the dispatch alone was insufficient. It should have run the teacher-artifact linter independently on both replay and cold-retest artifacts before sending either to the append boundary.
The harness behaved correctly by rejecting the malformed exchange atomically, appending no replay exposure or learner response, sounding ALARM, and freezing the log.
Because the run ended during the first controlled gate, I must not use the four early correct selections to claim lesson acquisition or compare later capability.
alarm_assessment: The harness ALARM at sequence 31 was warranted and correctly terminal. After the licensed PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch at sequence 30, the first replay artifact declared exercise l001-p1-affirmative-model in phase affirmative even though that exercise belongs to presentation; it also did not preserve the required replay delivery, exact fork text, or exact script reference. The exchange was rejected atomically with zero events admitted from it, so the malformed replay did not become learner exposure. Primary root cause is luna_routine: incorrect serialization of a clearly mapped replay. A secondary orchestration/harness-preflight gap is that the broker validated the dispatch but failed to lint the replay and cold-retest artifacts independently before admission. The harness's final rejection and freeze were correct, not a harness integrity failure.

next_lesson_implications: Do not advance learner closure or commission a successor lesson from this run; preserve it as an alarm-frozen conductor and orchestration incident.

Repair PRESENT_AGAIN realization as a deterministic or tightly templated three-step micro-protocol: validate dispatch, materialize and lint the one mapped presentation turn, then materialize and lint the mapped cold retest.

For the failed fork item, require the replay artifact to preserve the presentation phase, exact fork delivery and text, and exact script reference from the frozen presentation item; require the cold artifact to preserve the affirmative phase and mapped cold-retest ID.

Make pre-admission lint mandatory for every generated replay and cold-retest artifact, not only for the tool dispatch. Reject locally before any append attempt if phase, exercise, delivery, text, script reference, or assets differ from the frozen contract.
Run a focused unit rehearsal of one incorrect controlled item through PRESENT_AGAIN, replay, and cold retest before repeating the complete lesson in a new linked run.
After the micro-protocol passes, rerun the full frozen lesson from the beginning in a new linked directory; do not resume or overwrite this terminal run.
